initial_request: Compare online travel, hotels, airlines, and consumer staples. Explain why online travel is currently leading, when the other sectors could overtake it, and prepare a news reaction note plus a sector watch update.

constraints: Do not confirm a bearish view on online travel before the relevant booking and demand news is verified.
If rotation_status is ambiguous, do not lock into a single winner sector.
Include online_travel, hotels, airlines, and consumer_staples in the comparison set.
The recommended_sector_weights should stay close to a total of 1.0.

task_dependencies.reason: Travel demand news should be verified before the sector stance is updated.
The competing sectors should be compared before the final watchlist is locked.
The added defensive-sector viewpoint should be incorporated before the final watchlist is locked.

reference_data.headline_summary: baseline checks still favor online travel on resilient booking trends
reference_data.baseline_stability_reason: Booking trends and pricing discipline still support online travel leadership while broader discretionary demand remains intact.
sector_links: If consumer confidence softens, hotels can hold up better than online travel if group bookings stay firm.
If the growth scare deepens, capital can rotate from travel exposure into consumer staples.
reference_data.budget_unit: portfolio weight points (100 = full sector allocation budget)

correlation_map.note: Hotels can lag less if direct and group demand remain healthy despite softer online booking momentum.
Staples can outperform if the market de-risks from discretionary travel exposure.
Fuel and macro shocks tend to separate cyclical travel from defensive staples.

reference_data.decision_goal: decide whether to reduce online travel exposure and raise consumer staples or hotel exposure
